clusters.title: The runtime ledger is in v1 with no row in 00 0.5, no success criterion and no journey, and it sits on the build path before romeu run.
clusters.scenario: A scope reviewer cannot say what the ledger is for in the product's own terms; S7's journeys pass with the ledger broken; if the plan slips, nothing says the ledger tasks (T063 to T065, T071, T072) may move, so they stay on the critical path before run.
clusters.change: Operator decides one of two: (a) move the ledger out of v1 as one Deferred row ('the runtime ledger (13; ADR 0006 stays the design); until then julieta state (08 8.2) and command stderr are the record; reopened by the first docs/lessons.md entry naming an in-sandbox failure julieta state could not reconstruct, or a second machine'), keep 13 as a designed-not-built page like 06 6.6, and remove the two mounts (03 3.3), the ingest steps (04 4.2, 08 8.5), I31 to I33 and the ledger doctor rows; or (b) keep it, add a 00 0.5 row 'runtime ledger: ADR 0006, I31 to I33, the lessons loop of 12 12.7', and add to ADR 0006 the 'not in v1' alternative with why it was rejected. Either way, no cut-line list is added to 00 0.5: the cut order is a plan concern.
clusters.cost: (a) about a page of deletions across index, 03, 04, 05, 08, 12 and the plan; (b) one row and one ADR paragraph.
clusters.operator_reason: Changes the v1 scope (00 0.5) and ADR 0006 (Alternatives considered), both of which only the operator decides.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend (b) unless the operator wants a smaller v1: one 00 0.5 row and ADR 0006's missing 'not in v1' alternative close the traceability gap at low cost; (a) is the right call if the ledger has no first-day reader the operator can name. The cut-line part of L9-20 is not taken into the spec.

clusters.title: The generic product carries one person's migration (julieta memory import and verify, the import/ entry, the memory-entry digest kind, the repo evidence kind, tools/ci acceptance --file, the C1 hugo check), justified in 00 0.5 by the maintainer's own pre-v1 memory.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter (00 0.2) reads 0.5's 'memory entries written before v1 are imported when v1 is adopted' and reference pages documenting commands and an evidence kind that apply to nobody but the author, and an acceptance that checks a tool they do not use.
clusters.change: Operator decides: (a) delete import and verify, the import/ allowlist entry, the memory-entry digest kind, the repo evidence kind, --file and C1, and do the one-time import with a script in the operator's config repo (02 2.2 already allows an operator acceptance.json there); or (b) keep them, rewrite the 00 0.5 cell as a general need ('importing memory written before adoption, by another tool or an earlier setup, once; operator-only'), and mark the commands operator-only in 04 4.3.
clusters.cost: (a) deletions in 00, 03, 04, 08, 10, 11 and the plan (T058, parts of T082 and T090), one script outside the product; (b) one cell and one marker.
clusters.operator_reason: The 00 0.5 row records a maintainer decision ('the maintainer decided ... and kept tools/ci acceptance --file'); removing or narrowing these features changes the v1 scope.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend (a): the import runs once, on one machine, and a config-repo script serves it without the product carrying six concepts for good. If the operator keeps them, apply (b), which is L10-28's change.

clusters.title: The secondary user's need ('the product is generic') traces to no criterion, invariant or journey; every acceptance runs with the maintainer's own config repo.
clusters.scenario: v1.0.0 passes S1 to S11; a stranger with their own config repo runs J1 and stops at the first sync; no criterion ever ran without the author's config.
clusters.change: In the 00 0.2 Secondary row, replace the v1 support cell with: 'generic by design (no personal values in code); v1 acceptance runs only with the maintainer's config repo and examples/, so a fresh adopter's first run is not tested; onboarding documented; no support promise'. Add no S12 now; add a Deferred row: 'an acceptance run from a fresh account without the reference config repo; until then examples/ is the only non-maintainer config the tests use; reopened by the first issue from an adopter blocked in J1 to J3b'.
clusters.cost: One cell and one Deferred row.
clusters.operator_reason: Whether v1 gains a user-facing criterion (S12) is a scope decision across R8-index-22, R8-00-3 and R8-09-2; routed with them to the operator as SC16 by the gate review of the round page.
clusters.resolution_text: State the limit in 00 0.2 and defer the stranger-run criterion with a trigger, instead of adding S12 and a block B sitting now; adding S12 would be a scope change the operator may still ask for.

clusters.title: The objective's 'nothing sandbox-only is lost' has no scope, while 08 8.5 salvages a closed list (recorded repos, ignored files within the cap, the agent profile's state paths, transcripts on request).
clusters.scenario: An agent clones a second repo into $HOME/scratch and keeps a database in /tmp; romeu rm reports salvage complete and removes the sandbox; both are gone and the operator had read 0.1 as a promise.
clusters.change: Rewrite the 0.1 bullet: 'nothing that salvage covers is lost when a sandbox is recreated or removed: the recorded repos (worktrees, local refs, stashes, ignored files within the cap) and the agent's state paths (08 8.5); anything else in the sandbox is not kept'. Make the 00 0.2 Primary 'Needs' cell and the first 00 0.5 row quote the same words. Add to 08 8.5 one short list 'Not salvaged' (paths outside the recorded repos and state paths, unrecorded clones, /tmp, installed plugins, multiplexer scrollback), cited from 0.1. No new 05 5.4 row.
clusters.cost: One bullet, two cells, one list in 08 8.5.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the qualifier and the 'Not salvaged' list; drop the proposed 05 5.4 residual-risk row (it would change the accepted-risk list) and leave the 08 8.4 sentence to the page-08 consolidation.

clusters.title: The objective says nothing an agent wrote is ever executed on the host, while personal kits are agent-authored and sbx builds them at create, and no probe records where a kit's install step runs.
clusters.scenario: A personal kit's install step runs on the host Docker engine at sbx env run; the gate showed the diff and the operator approved it, so the code was reviewed, which is a weaker claim than 'never executed'.
clusters.change: Reword the second half of the 0.1 gate bullet to 'nothing an agent wrote runs on the host unless the operator approved it at that gate', and the 00 0.2 Primary cell to 'no unreviewed host code execution from agent output'. Add one observation to the A11 probe in 11: 'where a kit install step executes (host engine or microVM), as the harness can observe'; when it shows the microVM, the stronger sentence may return.
clusters.cost: Two phrases and one probe observation.
clusters.resolution_text: Weaken the universal to what the design guarantees and attach the measurement that could restore it; no new mechanism.

clusters.title: 00 0.5 claims every v1 feature traces to a criterion, an invariant, a journey or a named need, but its table is a sample (romeu pull, retire, recreate, julieta lock, spec validate, pin workload and others have no row) and justifies julieta handoff list by 'kept in v1 by the maintainer' alone.
clusters.scenario: The scope skeptic asks what romeu retire is for; 0.5 cannot answer and its universal cannot be checked, so the table cannot be used to cut anything.
clusters.change: Replace the 0.5 opening with: 'The table lists the v1 features whose need was questioned in review, each with what needs it; a command without a row here is justified by the journey or invariant its row in 04 cites. A feature with neither is deferred with a row in Deferred decisions.' Replace the handoff list cell with the need: 'an agent choosing which handoff to read when a repo holds more than one (08)'; if no such need stands, delete the command and its row.
clusters.resolution_text: Weaken the universal to what the table is and move the burden to the 04 command rows, instead of adding about twelve rows and a check; the 'marked v1.1' clause goes with R8-00-7.

clusters.title: The 'v1.1' row of 00 0.5 holds four items (native egress queue in status, handoff --list filters, a Remote-SSH helper, a registry credential) with no trigger and no interim, and the registry credential also lives as Q23 under a different rule.
clusters.scenario: Nothing reopens any of the four; one item lives in two tables with two rules, beside a principle that calls a deferral without a row an oversight.
clusters.change: Delete the v1.1 row of 00 0.5 and the v1.1 parenthesis of 07 7.5. Add Deferred rows: native egress queue in status (until then sbx's own approval list, named in 07 7.5; reopened by the first issue from a user who resolved a native approval without knowing it existed); handoff --list filters (until then the unfiltered list; reopened by the first issue asking for a filter); Remote-SSH helper (until then the manual steps of the guide; reopened by the first issue asking for it); registry credential (merge Q23 into this row, keeping its trigger text, and delete Q23).
clusters.cost: Three new rows, one merged row, two deletions.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed: one table, one rule, every deferral with its interim and trigger.

clusters.title: S8 and run --timings justify each other: the flag exists only for the criterion and the criterion's evidence is the flag, so a schema, a CI median-of-5 test and a probe measure budgets (2 s, 3 s) with no stated origin.
clusters.scenario: A first user never types --timings; the CI timing test is asserted never to flake, so a slow runner blocks a merge on a number chosen before any code ran.
clusters.change: Operator decides whether --timings stays in v1. If not: keep S8 as a measured property of the host suite (B5 times the runs in the harness), delete --timings, run-timings.v1 (03 3.13, 02 2.1) and the CI assertion, and delete the '--timings' row of 00 0.5. In both cases add to S8: 'the 2 s and 3 s bounds are starting values; the first B5 measurement confirms or resets them'.
clusters.cost: Deletions in 00, 02, 03, 04, 10 and the index; one sentence in S8.
clusters.operator_reason: Removing --timings deletes a 00 0.5 row and a v1 feature, which is a scope change; the S8 sentence alone stays inside the spec text.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend dropping --timings and timing in the harness; apply the starting-values sentence to S8 regardless.

clusters.title: 00 0.6 is a 35-line analysis of an external report (with page numbers) for a user v1 does not serve, on the page that decides v1 scope, and its 'partial' rows read as commitments.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter reads 0.6 as a roadmap and a planner reads 'partial' as half-done work; the report publishes v2026.2 with new page numbers and the scope page goes stale.
clusters.change: Move the 0.6 table, its preamble and the 'honest count' paragraph verbatim to docs/notes/dora-roi-report.md (a docs note, not a spec page). Replace 0.6 with three sentences: 'v1 serves one developer and has no team feature. The maintainer's premise is that teams adopting AI-assisted development come next; the analysis of the DORA and Google Cloud report behind that premise is in docs/notes/dora-roi-report.md. Recording the inputs of the report's return model is a deferred decision with its trigger.' Set the 00 0.2 'Future: teams' v1 support cell to 'none; see 0.6'. The 12 12.10 half of L3-24 belongs to page 12.
clusters.cost: About 60 lines moved, three sentences, one cell.
clusters.resolution_text: Move the analysis to a docs note and keep a three-sentence 0.6, keeping the teams row in 0.2 with 'none'; the 12 12.10 trim is left to the page-12 consolidation.

clusters.title: 00 0.3 says a run-layout renderer interface exists as the hedge against herdr, a pre-1.0 project on the path of every romeu run, but the interface is specified nowhere and no row says what happens if herdr is abandoned.
clusters.scenario: herdr breaks its protocol or stops being maintained; the 'interface' turns out to map straight to layout.apply, and a second renderer means redesigning attach, stale-layout detection and the pane runner, with nothing having reopened the question.
clusters.change: Rewrite the 0.3 bullet: 'tmux and cmux renderers. The run layout format (03 3.2) names no multiplexer; herdr is the one renderer, and the renderer interface is designed with the second one.' Drop the 'renderer interface exists' wording from 12 12.9 to match. Add a Deferred row: 'a second run-layout renderer and its interface; until then herdr, pinned by version and sha256, is the one renderer; reopened by a herdr release that breaks the protocol number A13 recorded, a CVE in herdr, or six months without a herdr release'.
clusters.cost: One bullet, one phrase in 12 12.9, one Deferred row.
clusters.resolution_text: Delete the unsupported 'interface exists' claim and carry the hedge as a Deferred row with an abandonment trigger, instead of specifying a renderer contract now.

clusters.title: The prerequisites a stranger needs are not stated: how the agent logs in inside the sandbox, mise in each worked-on repo (07 7.2), GitHub for the config repo's CI, and Keychain items for secrets.
clusters.scenario: An adopter installs sbx, git and gh per 12 12.8, runs J1 to step 7, and the agent pane asks for a login the spec never mentions; their repos have no mise.toml, so julieta setup installs nothing and panes fail on missing tools.
clusters.change: Extend the README prerequisites outline in 12 12.8 with: a Claude Code login done inside the sandbox at first run, a mise.toml in each repo whose tools julieta setup installs, a GitHub account for the config repo's CI, and Keychain items for the secret names. Add to the 00 0.2 Primary 'Needs' cell: 'prerequisites listed once in 12 12.8'. Say in 09 J1 at which step the agent login happens. The 0.3 audience list is not added.
clusters.cost: Four outline lines, one cell phrase, one J1 sentence.
clusters.resolution_text: List the prerequisites once in 12 12.8 and point to it; drop the new 0.3 audience list, which would widen the non-goals (a scope change) and mostly repeats existing ones.

clusters.title: 00 0.4 and S11 cover the repository's files, not the release archives: nothing says an archive carries COPYING and the notices of statically linked modules, and nothing checks a new dependency's license against GPL-3.0-only.
clusters.scenario: v1.0.0's darwin archive holds only the binary; the notices of its Go modules do not travel with it, and a later dependency with an incompatible license passes every check.
clusters.change: Add to 00 0.4: 'Each release archive contains COPYING and a third-party notices file that tools/release build generates from the module graph; a tools/ci license step fails a module whose license is not on an allowlist compatible with GPL-3.0-only.' Add the notices file to S1's asset description and the license step to the 10 10.2 check list.
clusters.cost: One generator step in tools/release, one allowlist check, three sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed: a deterministic check is the right home for license compatibility.

clusters.title: The same person is 'operator', 'maintainer', 'developer' and 'user' across the pages, none of the four is in the vocabulary, and the sentence relating them is only in ADR 0008 Context.
clusters.scenario: A second adopter reads 'the maintainer's approval' in 05 5.3 and 'the operator decided' in 05 5.4 and concludes the product has two roles, one of which they must find.
clusters.change: Add to 01 1.7 three rows: operator (the person who runs romeu on a host, owns host settings and answers gates), maintainer (the person who merges and releases the product repository), developer (00 0.2's name for the operator as a user); and one sentence: 'today one person holds both roles'. In 00 0.2 the Primary row reads 'a developer (the operator, 01 1.7)'. Each page uses each word in its sense only; the word pass belongs to the pages that use them.
clusters.cost: Three rows, one sentence, a word pass.
clusters.resolution_text: Define the words once in 01 1.7 and link from 00 0.2; 'user' stays plain English, not a fourth term. Shared with the page-01 consolidation, which owns the rows.

clusters.title: No user row names the organization whose code passes through the tree, and 0.6 says memory answers 'loss of familiarity' without saying memory is machine-local and leaves with the developer.
clusters.scenario: A team adopts the product for codebase familiarity; a developer leaves and their memory about the employer's repos stays on their laptop.
clusters.change: Add under the 00 0.2 table one sentence: 'The organization that owns the code is not a user v1 serves; what the tool stores about a repository, and where, is listed in 08.' In the familiarity row's Gap cell (moved to the docs note by R8-00-9) add: 'memory is machine-local (Q14) and outside the repository, so it leaves with the developer'.
clusters.resolution_text: State the limit in a sentence instead of adding a users row with a support promise.

clusters.title: Product kits are GPL-3.0-only and users put personal kits in their config repo, but nothing says what a personal kit copied from a product kit is licensed under.
clusters.scenario: An adopter copies kits/os-base into a private config repo as a start and does not know whether holding GPL files there matters.
clusters.change: Add to 00 0.4: 'A personal kit copied from a product kit stays GPL-3.0-only; to start a kit without that, copy the example kits under examples/kits/ (CC0-1.0).'
clusters.resolution_text: State the license outcome in one sentence; examples/ already carries kits (02 2.1), so no new example is needed.
